lessons.title: Control Plans & SPC Charts
lessons.content_md:
# Control Plans & SPC Charts

## Control Plan

A living document that ensures improvements are **sustained** after the project ends.

### Components

| Element | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Process step | Key step being controlled | Data entry validation |
| CTQ | What's being measured | Error rate per batch |
| Specification | Acceptable limits | <2% error rate |
| Measurement method | How it's measured | Automated system check |
| Frequency | How often | Every batch (100 forms) |
| Reaction plan | What to do if out of spec | Re-train, root cause review |
| Owner | Who is responsible | QA Lead |

## Statistical Process Control (SPC)

### Control Charts

Control charts monitor process stability over time:

```
UCL ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─  Upper Control Limit
      ·  ·     ·  ·  ·
CL  ─ ─ ─ · ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ · ─ ─ ─   Center Line (Mean)
            ·        ·     ·
LCL ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─  Lower Control Limit
```

### Types of Control Charts
- **X-bar and R chart**: For continuous data (averages and ranges)
- **p-chart**: For proportion defective
- **c-chart**: For count of defects per unit
- **np-chart**: For number of defective items

### Interpreting Control Charts

Process is **out of control** if:
1. A point falls outside control limits
2. 7 consecutive points on one side of center line (run)
3. 7 consecutive points trending up or down
4. Cyclic patterns

## Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)

Document the improved process so anyone can follow it:
- Step-by-step instructions with screenshots
- Decision trees for exception handling
- Escalation procedures
- Review and update schedule

lessons.title: Reflection Quiz: Deploy Phase
lessons.content_md:
# Reflection Quiz

Test your understanding of the Control/Deploy phase.

quiz_data.question: A control chart signals a process is 'out of control' when:
options: All points are near the center line
A point falls outside the control limits
The mean shifts by less than 1 sigma

quiz_data.question: A p-chart is used to monitor:
What is the purpose of a Control Plan?
options: Ensure improvements are sustained after project ends

quiz_data.question: How many consecutive points on one side of the center line indicate a 'run'?
SOPs are important in the Control phase because:
options: They document the improved process for consistent execution
They eliminate the need for training
